cell.label: Purulent endocervical exudate OR increased friability of endocervical mucosa. Signs of PID?
Examine vaginal saline prep; test for GC and Chlamydia. Trichomonads present?
Treat presumptively for Chlamydia. If follow-up is insecure or if a test other than NAAT is used.
Consider presumptive treatment for GC if the prevalence is high (>5%) in the patient's population.
Consider testing for trichomonas by culture or antigen testing.
Await results of GC and Chlamydia testing.

footnotes.footnote: Abbreviations: GC, gonorrhea; NAAT, nucleic acid amplification test; PID, pelvic inflammatory disease.
Adapted from Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. http://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment. Sexually Transmitted Disease Treatment Guidelines.
